data.title: Clay idols from Budmerice (Early Bronze Age, the Maďarovce culture)
data.excerpt: Another article by Slovak archaeologists, this time on finds of cult objects of the Early Bronze Age recently discovered at the fortified settlement in Budmerice. Pavol Jelínek, Jana Mellnerová Šuteková and Július Vavák present a fragment of a loaf-shaped idol, an atypical flat clay idol and further clay figurines whose function remains unknown.
data.metaTitle: Clay idols from Budmerice – the Maďarovce culture
data.metaDescription: Cult clay idols of the Early Bronze Age discovered at the fortified settlement of the Maďarovce culture in Budmerice, excavated by SAHI and the Pezinok museum.

children.text: Here is another article by Slovak archaeologists. This time it concerns finds of interesting cult objects of the Early Bronze Age that were recently discovered at the fortified settlement in Budmerice. The article comes from the archaeologists P. Jelínek, J. Mellnerová Šuteková and Július Vavák, who are carrying out archaeological excavation at this fortified settlement.

Since 2010 the SAHI civic association, in cooperation with the Lesser Carpathian Museum in Pezinok, has been carrying out systematic archaeological excavation of the fortified settlement of the Maďarovce culture in Budmerice (figs 1, 2). Besides other finds, the excavation of this multi-period site has produced clay artefacts that can be interpreted as idols.

In 2010, in feature 2, besides other finds (vessels, human bones, casting moulds, burnt grain and others) a fragment of a loaf-shaped idol (the so-called Brotleibidol) was also found. According to the typology (figs 5, 6) drawn up by M. Bartík and R. Bača (1999), given the fragmentary state of the find this is probably an idol of the type with a simple round impression (fig. 3). The number of transverse ribs with impressions cannot be determined; only one has survived on the fragment. The closest analogy is a similar, almost completely preserved idol with two impressions (fig. 4), which was found at the site in the past (Bartík 2012, 26). Loaf-shaped idols are usually interpreted in connection with the Early Bronze Age cult. The find from feature 2 supports this interpretation; we interpret the contents of feature 2 as the sacred refuse of a (chthonic?) ritual (Jelínek, in press).

In March 2012 an atypical flat clay idol was found by chance at the site (fig. 7:1). Since this was a surface find from a multi-period site, its precise dating is possible only by means of analogies. So far the only one is a similar find from Radčice (Strakonice district) in southern Bohemia (fig. 7:2), dated to the Middle Bronze Age (Chvojka/Michálek 2006, 76 fig. 6). Provisionally and with reservations, the Budmerice idol can be dated to the Middle Bronze Age phase of the Maďarovce culture. Its function, as with the bread idols, remains unknown.

Fragments of wheels (fig. 8) can also be assigned to the idols, or rather to figurines with a non-profane meaning. Also of interest is a fragment of a figurine (a limb?, fig. 9) and clay axe-hammers (figs 10; 11). Since, however, they come from layers and from surface collection, more precise dating is not possible.
Pavol Jelínek, Jana Mellnerová Šuteková, Július Vavák: CLAY IDOLS FROM BUDMERICE
